note: State park beach campground at Point Mugu: one row of sites on the open sand on the ocean side of Pacific Coast Highway. Storms have taken several sites and the turnarounds, so the combined length limit is strictly enforced, and high tides flood the campground often; check tides with the park on arrival. Portable toilets only. --Claude

flags: STATUS: temporarily_closed - parks.ca.gov: 'Thornhill Broome Campground in Point Mugu State Park will be closed beginning 10/8/26 due to high tide.' ReserveCalifornia blocks every unreserved night 2026-11-28 through at least 2027-02-07; nights are free again in March and April 2027. No reopening date published.

WATERFRONT: stored 'coastal dunes' (not --AWH) -> recommend 'bayfront' on the Doheny 11631 precedent (open-ocean frontage on open sand, no road between). There is no dune field: the single row of paved back-in spurs sits on open beach sand with Pacific Coast Highway on the INLAND side, so the stored value's premise is wrong. Named sites: all 34 web units TB10-TB45 (less TB12/TB31), each tagged 'Proximity to Water: Oceanfront' on ReserveCalifornia and sold by the night at $35; the rest of the 59-site row (TB6-TB9, TB46-TB65) is the same row. Esri 2026-11-27: row centre ~34.0800,-119.0294, site row to wet sand ~50-55 m over a gentle open beach, nothing between (no road, lot, day-use or berm); the park says high tides flood the campground, so the high-water line reaches the row and the pads are only ~1-2 m above it. Replacement evidence: 'Esri 2026-11-27 + ReserveCalifornia: single row of paved spurs on open beach sand seaward of PCH, ~50-55 m to wet sand, high tides reach the row (parks.ca.gov), no dune field; all 34 web sites RC Oceanfront, nightly $35'. If the reviewer reads bayfront as bays-only, coastal walk is the fallback; coastal dunes should not stay.
